comparison: Perfect agreement on C1-C5. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the isolation and characterization of phages requiring fliF deletion for plaque formation. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the findings and describe the isolation approach as novel.
Perfect agreement on C6-C7. Both support the phylogenetic and morphological characterization. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these claims as part of the 'convincing' work without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on C8-C12. Both support the flagellar component analysis showing MS-ring specificity. Peer reviewers affirm the mutational analysis and note data 'strongly supports their conclusions.'

Perfect agreement on C13-C19. Both strongly support the c-di-GMP mechanism linking c-di-GMP levels to phage susceptibility. Peer reviewers explicitly describe the bidirectional manipulation experiments and characterize data as strongly supporting conclusions.

Perfect agreement on C20-C23. Both support the TnSeq findings identifying phosphodiesterase genes and reaffirming c-di-GMP involvement. Peer reviewers describe experiments as 'thoughtful and rational.'

Perfect agreement on C24-C30. Both strongly support Psl requirement through TnSeq, targeted deletions, and complementation. Peer reviewers and editor highlight Psl receptor identification as a key contribution.

Strong agreement on C31-C34 with peer review also covering C35-C37. Both support the reconciliation of plaque vs. attachment assays and Psl-dependent attachment. Peer reviewers accept findings without critique as part of 'thoughtful and rational' experiments.

Agreement on C35-C37 (attachment visualization and quantification). OpenEval focuses on these specific claims while peer review groups them with C31-C34. Both support the attachment data showing population-level differences.

Perfect agreement on C38-C43. Both support direct Psl-phage binding evidence from biochemical assays. Peer reviewers affirm direct binding and describe work as 'convincing,' noting molecular characterization as potential future work.

Strong agreement on C44-C47 (biofilm disruption). OpenEval focuses on these claims while peer review also includes C48-C49. Both support biofilm-targeting activity with peer reviewers explicitly affirming 'significant loss of biofilm biomass.'
Agreement on C48-C49 (bacterial killing in biofilms). OpenEval treats these separately while peer review groups with C44-C47. Both support the evidence for bacterial death vs. decolonization.

Perfect agreement on C50-C56. Both support in vivo efficacy in mouse keratitis model. Peer reviewers note bacterial burden reduction while observing keratitis did not fully resolve, presented as observation rather than critique.

Perfect agreement on C57-C60. Both support the mechanistic distinction from capsule-targeting phages and lack of depolymerase activity. Peer reviewers accept this characterization as part of 'convincing' work.

Strong agreement on C61-C64 with peer review also covering C66, C95-C96. Both support the synthesis of findings into coherent model and methodological implications. Peer reviewers emphasize the novel screening technique and importance of biofilm-mode screening.

Partial overlap on C65-C66 with peer review covering broader set including C61-C64, C95-C96. Both support broader implications for phage ecology. OpenEval focuses on C65-C68 while peer review emphasizes novel screening approach.

Partial overlap on C65 with peer review covering C65, C69-C70, C97-C98. Both support evolutionary and ecological implications. Peer reviewers affirm the generalizable isolation strategy and broader impact.

Strong agreement on C69-C72. Both support the generalizable isolation strategy and validation through Knedl phage. Peer reviewers describe the novel screening technique and highlight importance of biofilm-mode phage discovery.

Strong agreement on C73-C74 with peer review covering broader context (C73-C74, C99-C111). Both support therapeutic potential. Peer reviewers emphasize novel approach to biofilm control and relevance to multiple research areas.

Perfect agreement on C75-C78. Both support phage lifecycle characterization including turbid plaque morphology and lytic classification. Peer reviewers accept these observations as part of 'convincing' characterization.

Strong agreement on C82-C84 with peer review also covering C79-C81. Both support LPS involvement and ssg identification. Peer reviewers accept findings as part of mechanistic characterization with 'thoughtful and rational' experiments.

Strong agreement on C85-C87 with peer review covering broader c-di-GMP context (C85-C93). Both support the distinction between MS-ring and filament requirements. Peer reviewers affirm mechanistic insights from flagellar mutational analysis.

Strong agreement on C88-C93. Both support integration with c-di-GMP regulation knowledge and TnSeq identification of pch and bifA. Peer reviewers describe experiments as 'thoughtful and rational' with strongly supporting data.

Partial overlap on C95-C96 with peer review covering C61-C64, C66, C95-C96. Both support conclusions about methodological bias in phage discovery. Peer reviewers emphasize novel screening technique development.

Partial overlap on C97-C98 with peer review covering C65, C69-C70, C71-C72, C97-C98. Both support generalizability and future impact claims. Peer reviewers affirm broader implications for phage discovery.

Strong agreement on C99-C111 with peer review also covering C73-C74, C112. Both support background context establishing clinical problem and knowledge gap. Peer reviewers affirm therapeutic relevance and novel approach to biofilm control.

Near-perfect agreement on C113-C124 (missing only C112 from peer review). Both strongly support integrated findings linking Psl biology to biofilm-targeting properties. Editor and reviewers highlight this as key contribution of 'valuable study.'
